reason: While this passage does show God (through Moses) reproaching the Hebrew people for their disobedience—specifically saying 'How long will you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?'—this rebuke occurs in a context of divine provision, not great suffering. The people are being provided miraculous manna from heaven. The rebuke is directed at their violation of the Sabbath law (gathering manna on the seventh day when told not to), not at explaining or assigning blame for widespread suffering. The statement requires both elements: great suffering AND leaders blaming the people for it. This text contains only the latter element in isolation.
